Appeal: denial reviewable by petition within 30 days: An order denying a motion to dispose under the Act may be reviewed by petition for leave to appeal under Supreme Court Rule 306(a)(9), filed with a supporting record within 30 days. The appellate court must expedite any appeal from a denial, or from the trial court’s failure to rule within 90 days. Once a party appeals a ruling on the motion, all proceedings between all parties are stayed until the appeal ends (actions from 2026 on). A grant that ends the case is appealed as a final judgment (Rule 303). A grant disposing of fewer than all claims or parties needs a Rule 304(a) finding. Note: §17(b) refers to the time ‘under Section 20 to appeal,’ but §20 sets no appeal deadline, so use Rule 306’s 30 days. (Ill. S. Ct. R. 306(a)(9), (c); 735 ILCS 110/20(a), 110/17(b)–(c))

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Notice of appeal from final judgment
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Notice of appeal from final judgment: 30 days from Entry of final judgment, or entry of order disposing of last pending timely postjudgment motion (Ill. S. Ct. R. 303(a)(1)). Jurisdictional. Filed in the circuit court.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Motion for leave to file late notice of appeal
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Motion for leave to file late notice of appeal: 30 days from Expiration of the time to file the notice of appeal (R. 303(d)). Filed in the reviewing court with reasonable excuse, proposed notice, and fee.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Cross-appeal, separate appeal, or joining appeal
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Cross-appeal, separate appeal, or joining appeal: 10 days from Service of another party’s timely notice of appeal (or 30 days from judgment / last postjudgment order, whichever is later) (R. 303(a)(3)). Use whichever period ends later.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Serve notice of appeal and file notice of filing in reviewing court
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Serve notice of appeal and file notice of filing in reviewing court: 7 days from Filing of notice of appeal (R. 303(c)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Post-trial motion (jury case)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Post-trial motion (jury case): 30 days from Entry of judgment or discharge of jury without verdict (735 ILCS 5/2-1202(c)). Single motion; extensions must be granted within the 30 days.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Postjudgment motion (nonjury case)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Postjudgment motion (nonjury case): 30 days from Entry of judgment (735 ILCS 5/2-1203(a); R. 274). Only one postjudgment motion per judgment tolls the appeal time.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Rule 137 sanctions motion
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Rule 137 sanctions motion: 30 days from Entry of final judgment, or ruling on timely postjudgment motion (R. 137(b)). A pending Rule 137 claim keeps the judgment non-final absent a 304(a) finding.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Section 2-1401 petition for relief from judgment
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Section 2-1401 petition for relief from judgment: 730 days from Entry of the judgment (735 ILCS 5/2-1401(c)). Statute says 2 years; excludes disability, duress, and fraudulent concealment periods.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Notice of interlocutory appeal as of right and Rule 328 supporting record
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Notice of interlocutory appeal as of right and Rule 328 supporting record: 30 days from Entry of the interlocutory order (or denial of motion to vacate an ex parte order) (R. 307(a), (b)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Petition to review TRO ruling (and notice in circuit court)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Petition to review TRO ruling (and notice in circuit court): 2 days from Entry or denial of the TRO order (R. 307(d)(1)). Response due 2 days after petition; decision within 5 business days.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Petition for leave to appeal interlocutory order (Rule 306)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Petition for leave to appeal interlocutory order (Rule 306): 30 days from Entry of the order (R. 306(c)(1)). Includes denial of Citizen Participation Act motion (306(a)(9)). Custody petitions under 306(a)(5): 14 days.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Answer to Rule 306 petition
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Answer to Rule 306 petition: 21 days from Filing of the petition (R. 306(c)(2)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Application for leave to appeal certified question
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Application for leave to appeal certified question: 30 days from Entry of order or trial court’s Rule 308 statement, whichever is later (R. 308(b)). Answer due 21 days after the application’s due date.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Bond extension limit in circuit court
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Bond extension limit in circuit court: 45 days from Aggregate of circuit court extensions for filing appeal bond (R. 305(c)). Unless parties stipulate otherwise.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Docketing statement (appeal as of right)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Docketing statement (appeal as of right): 14 days from Filing of notice of appeal (R. 312(a)(1)). 7 days for Rule 307 appeals.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Record on appeal
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Record on appeal: 63 days from Filing of the (last) notice of appeal (R. 326). Extension motion before deadline or within 35 days after with reasonable excuse.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 35 days from Filing of the record on appeal (R. 343(a)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 35 days from Due date of appellant’s brief (R. 343(a)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Reply brief: 14 days from Due date of appellee’s brief (R. 343(a)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Interlocutory (Rule 307) appellant’s brief
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Interlocutory (Rule 307) appellant’s brief: 7 days from Filing of the Rule 328 supporting record (R. 307(c)). Appellee 7 days later; reply 7 days after that.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing: 21 days from Filing of the reviewing court’s judgment (R. 367(a)). Extensions disfavored.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Petition for leave to appeal to Supreme Court
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Petition for leave to appeal to Supreme Court: 35 days from Appellate Court judgment, or denial of timely rehearing petition / judgment on rehearing (R. 315(b)(1)). Extensions only in the most extreme and compelling circumstances.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Answer to petition for leave to appeal
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Answer to petition for leave to appeal: 21 days from Expiration of the time to file the petition (R. 315(f)). Optional; no reply allowed.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Election to stand on PLA or file brief
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Election to stand on PLA or file brief: 14 days from Order allowing leave to appeal (R. 315(h)). Additional brief due 35 days after leave allowed.

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Mandate issues (earliest)
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Mandate issues (earliest): 35 days from Entry of judgment or order denying rehearing (R. 368(a)).

docs.t: Illinois appeal deadline — Motion for original submission date after e-filing rejection
docs.x: Illinois appellate deadline. Motion for original submission date after e-filing rejection: 5 days from Notice of rejection (court days) (R. 9(f)(1)). Court days, not calendar days.

docs.t: Indiana — The notice of appeal is filed with the appellate Clerk, not the trial court
docs.x: Indiana land mine. The notice of appeal is filed with the appellate Clerk, not the trial court: The notice of appeal is filed with the Clerk of the Indiana Supreme Court, Court of Appeals and Tax Court within 30 days after the final judgment is noted in the Chronological Case Summary, with the $250 fee. A late notice forfeits the appeal (except under Post-Conviction Rule 2). (Ind. App. R. 2(D), 9(A)(1), (A)(5), 9(E))

docs.t: Indiana — Motion to correct error: deemed denial starts the clock
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Motion to correct error: deemed denial starts the clock: After a timely motion to correct error, the notice of appeal is due 30 days after the ruling or 30 days after the motion is deemed denied under T.R. 53.3, whichever comes first. Do not wait for a written ruling after the deemed-denial date passes. (Ind. App. R. 9(A)(1); Ind. T.R. 53.3(A))

docs.t: Indiana — Some issues must be raised in a motion to correct error
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Some issues must be raised in a motion to correct error: A motion to correct error is generally optional, but it is required to raise newly discovered evidence (including jury misconduct) or a claim that a jury verdict is excessive or inadequate. It is due 30 days after entry of final judgment is noted in the CCS, and that time cannot be extended. (Ind. T.R. 59(A), (C); Ind. T.R. 6(C))

docs.t: Indiana — Money-payment orders are appealable now, or the chance may be lost
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Money-payment orders are appealable now, or the chance may be lost: Interlocutory orders for the payment of money, to compel execution of a document or delivery of securities, for sale or delivery of real property, on preliminary injunctions and receivers, and transferring or refusing to transfer venue under T.R. 75 are appealable as of right within 30 days after the order is noted in the CCS. Other interlocutory orders need a motion for trial-court certification within 30 days and a motion in the Court of Appeals within 30 days after certification. (Ind. App. R. 14(A), (B)(1)(a), (B)(2)(a))

docs.t: Indiana — Change-of-judge window is short and one-time
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Change-of-judge window is short and one-time: The automatic change of judge must be sought within 10 days after the issues are first closed on the merits (typically the answer or reply). Miss it and you need a personally verified motion showing newly discovered grounds; each party gets only one change of judge and one change of county in the case. (Ind. T.R. 76(B)–(D))

docs.t: Indiana — Automatic 30-day extension to answer, but only if noticed on time
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Automatic 30-day extension to answer, but only if noticed on time: A party may get one automatic 30-day enlargement to respond to a complaint or other pleading by filing a notice stating the original and new due dates on or before the original due date. Responses to pleadings and motions are otherwise due 20 days after service, replies 14 days after the response, and 3 days are added only for service by U.S. mail. (Ind. T.R. 6(B), (D), (G))

docs.t: Indiana — Midnight deadline in the court’s time zone
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Midnight deadline in the court’s time zone: Indiana has counties in two time zones, and an e-filing is timely only if completed before midnight in the time zone of the court where the case is filed (or pending, on appeal). (Ind. T.R. 87(H); Ind. App. R. 68(I))

docs.t: Indiana — No extensions for rehearing or transfer petitions
docs.x: Indiana land mine. No extensions for rehearing or transfer petitions: A petition for rehearing is due 30 days after the decision and a petition to transfer 45 days after the decision (or 30 days after a rehearing ruling). No extension is allowed, and the 3-day mail extension does not apply. (Ind. App. R. 35(C), 54(B), 57(C))

docs.t: Indiana — Pre-2023 memorandum decisions are not citable
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Pre-2023 memorandum decisions are not citable: Unpublished Court of Appeals memorandum decisions issued before January 1, 2023 may not be cited to any court except for res judicata, collateral estoppel, or law of the case. Those issued on or after January 1, 2023 may be cited for persuasive value. A party may move to publish within 15 days of the decision. (Ind. App. R. 65(B), (D))

docs.t: Indiana — Summary judgment lives or dies on ‘designation’
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Summary judgment lives or dies on ‘designation’: The opponent has 30 days to respond, each side must specifically designate the evidence it relies on, and the court considers only designated material. A summary-judgment ruling will not be reversed on a fact issue that was not specifically designated to the trial court. (Ind. T.R. 56(C), (H))

docs.t: Indiana — Pro hac vice: $300 per case, good-standing certificates under 30 days old, residency bar
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Pro hac vice: $300 per case, good-standing certificates under 30 days old, residency bar: Temporary admission requires Indiana co-counsel who signs everything, a $300 per-case fee paid before filing the petition, certificates of good standing from every admitting state issued within 30 days, and the applicant may not be an Indiana resident or regularly practicing or employed in Indiana. (Ind. Admis. Disc. R. 3, § 2(a)–(b))

docs.t: Indiana — Discovery motions need a recited conference
docs.x: Indiana land mine. Discovery motions need a recited conference: Before filing a discovery motion, a party must make a reasonable effort to resolve the dispute and state in the motion the date, time, and place of that effort and who took part, or the court may deny the motion. Discovery requests must also be served in an editable word-processing format. (Ind. T.R. 26(F), (A)(1))

docs.t: Indiana anti-SLAPP — Statute: Ind. Code ch. 34-7-7 (1998)
docs.x: Indiana anti-SLAPP. Statute: Ind. Code ch. 34-7-7 (1998): Indiana’s anti-SLAPP law makes it a defense to a civil action that the act or omission complained of was (1) in furtherance of the person’s right of petition or free speech under the U.S. or Indiana Constitution in connection with a public issue or issue of public interest, and (2) taken in good faith and with a reasonable basis in law and fact. ‘Claim’ includes a lawsuit, cause of action, petition, complaint, cross-claim, counterclaim, or any other pleading seeking legal or equitable relief, and ‘person’ includes any legal entity. The chapter does not apply to enforcement actions brought for the State by the attorney general, a prosecutor, or another public prosecutor. The chapter has not been amended since it was added by P.L.114-1998 (it is not a UPEPA statute). (Ind. Code §§ 34-7-7-1 to -5, -10)

docs.t: Indiana anti-SLAPP — Procedure: motion to dismiss treated as summary judgment; 180-day outer limit
docs.x: Indiana anti-SLAPP. Procedure: motion to dismiss treated as summary judgment; 180-day outer limit: The defendant raises the defense by a motion to dismiss under the chapter, which must state with specificity the public issue or issue of public interest that prompted the act. The court must treat it as a summary-judgment motion, set a reasonable expedited period of no more than 180 days to rule, and set limits for discovery needed to respond. Filing the motion stays all discovery except discovery relevant to the motion. The court decides on the pleadings and affidavits filed and discovered in the expedited proceeding, and must grant the motion if the movant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the act on which the claim is based is a lawful act in furtherance of petition or speech rights. The statute sets no deadline for filing the motion; check case law on timing before relying

docs.t: Indiana anti-SLAPP — Mandatory fees for a prevailing defendant; fees against a frivolous movant
docs.x: Indiana anti-SLAPP. Mandatory fees for a prevailing defendant; fees against a frivolous movant: A defendant who prevails on the motion is entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs. If the court finds the motion frivolous or solely intended to cause unnecessary delay, the plaintiff is entitled to reasonable fees and costs to answer it. (Ind. Code §§ 34-7-7-7, -8)

docs.t: Indiana anti-SLAPP — Appeal: only an express right if the court fails to rule in 30 days
docs.x: Indiana anti-SLAPP. Appeal: only an express right if the court fails to rule in 30 days: The court must act within 30 days after the submission of the evidence discovered in the expedited period. If it does not, the movant may appeal based on the failure to rule. The chapter gives no express interlocutory appeal from an order denying the motion; absent another route, a denial would need trial-court certification and Court of Appeals acceptance under App.R. 14(B). Confirm current case law on appealability before advising. (Ind. Code § 34-7-7-9(e)–(f); Ind. App. R. 14(B))

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Notice of Appeal (final judgment)
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Notice of Appeal (final judgment): 30 days from Entry of the final judgment noted in the CCS (Ind. App. R. 9(A)(1)). Filed with the appellate Clerk with a $250 fee. Untimely notice forfeits the appeal.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion to correct error
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion to correct error: 30 days from Entry of the final judgment noted in the CCS (Ind. T.R. 59(C)). Cannot be extended (T.R. 6(C)). Opposing statement due 15 days after service.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Notice of Appeal after a motion to correct error
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Notice of Appeal after a motion to correct error: 30 days from Ruling noted in the CCS or deemed denial under T.R. 53.3, whichever is first (Ind. App. R. 9(A)(1); Ind. T.R. 53.3). Deemed denied if not set within 45 days, or not ruled on within 30 days after hearing or 45 days after filing without a hearing.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Notice of Appeal (agency judicial review in the Court of Appeals)
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Notice of Appeal (agency judicial review in the Court of Appeals): 30 days from Date of the agency order, ruling, or decision (Ind. App. R. 9(A)(3)). Applies notwithstanding any statute to the contrary.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Interlocutory appeal of right
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Interlocutory appeal of right: 30 days from Notation of the interlocutory order in the CCS (Ind. App. R. 14(A)). Includes orders for the payment of money and preliminary injunctions.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion to certify interlocutory order (trial court)
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion to certify interlocutory order (trial court): 30 days from Notation of the order in the CCS (Ind. App. R. 14(B)(1)(a)). Response due 15 days after service; deemed denied if the court does not act within 30 days.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion asking the Court of Appeals to accept interlocutory appeal
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion asking the Court of Appeals to accept interlocutory appeal: 30 days from Notation of the trial court’s certification in the CCS (Ind. App. R. 14(B)(2)(a)). Response due 15 days after service.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Notice of Appeal after acceptance of discretionary interlocutory appeal
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Notice of Appeal after acceptance of discretionary interlocutory appeal: 15 days from Court of Appeals order accepting jurisdiction (Ind. App. R. 14(B)(3), (C)(5)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Class-certification interlocutory appeal motion
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Class-certification interlocutory appeal motion: 30 days from Notation of the class-certification order in the CCS (Ind. App. R. 14(C)(1)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Transcript payment agreement with the court reporter
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Transcript payment agreement with the court reporter: 10 days from Filing of the Notice of Appeal (Ind. App. R. 9(H)). Court reporter may require a 50% deposit.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Clerk’s Record assembled
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Clerk’s Record assembled: 30 days from Filing of the Notice of Appeal (Ind. App. R. 10(B)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Transcript filed by court reporter
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Transcript filed by court reporter: 45 days from Filing of the Notice of Appeal (Ind. App. R. 11(B)). Extensions by the reporter’s motion under App.R. 35(A).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 30 days from Service of the Notice of Completion of Clerk’s Record (if Transcript complete or not requested), otherwise of the Notice of Completion of Transcript (Ind. App. R. 45(B)(1)). The 3-day mail extension does not apply. Appendix due the same day (App.R. 49(A)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 30 days from Service of the appellant’s brief (Ind. App. R. 45(B)(2)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Reply brief: 15 days from Service of the appellee’s brief (Ind. App. R. 45(B)(3)). 30 days if it is also the cross-appellee’s brief.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Cross-appellant’s reply brief
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Cross-appellant’s reply brief: 15 days from Service of the appellant’s reply brief (Ind. App. R. 45(B)(4)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion for extension of time
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion for extension of time: 7 days from Before the deadline expires (at least 7 days before) (Ind. App. R. 35(A)). Never after the deadline; none for rehearing or transfer.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion for oversized brief
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion for oversized brief: 15 days from Before the brief is due (at least 15 days before) (Ind. App. R. 44(B)). State words requested, not pages.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Motion to publish a memorandum decision
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Motion to publish a memorandum decision: 15 days from Entry of the decision (Ind. App. R. 65(B)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing: 30 days from The decision (Ind. App. R. 54(B)). No extensions; mail extension does not apply.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Petition to transfer (no rehearing sought)
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Petition to transfer (no rehearing sought): 45 days from The adverse Court of Appeals decision (Ind. App. R. 57(C)(1)). $125 fee (App.R. 56(B)). No extensions.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Petition to transfer (after rehearing)
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Petition to transfer (after rehearing): 30 days from Court of Appeals disposition of the petition for rehearing (Ind. App. R. 57(C)(2)). No extensions.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Response to petition to transfer
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Response to petition to transfer: 20 days from Service of the petition (Ind. App. R. 57(D)). Mail extension may apply; no other extension.

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Reply on transfer
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Reply on transfer: 10 days from Service of the response (Ind. App. R. 57(E)).

docs.t: Indiana appeal deadline — Cure of a Notice of Defect
docs.x: Indiana appellate deadline. Cure of a Notice of Defect: 10 days from Date of the Notice of Defect (business days) (Ind. App. R. 23(D)(1)(a)). 20 business days for unrepresented incarcerated persons.

docs.t: Kansas — Filing alone may not stop the limitations clock
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Filing alone may not stop the limitations clock: An action counts as commenced on the filing date only if service (or first publication) is made within 90 days after filing, extendable once by 30 days for good cause. Otherwise it is commenced only on the date of service. Relation back for a new defendant also depends on notice within the limitations period plus that service window. (K.S.A. 60-203(a)-(b); 60-215(c)(3))

docs.t: Kansas — Caption and damages pleading rules
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Caption and damages pleading rules: The petition must state below the caption that it is filed under chapter 60 (“Petition Pursuant to K.S.A. Chapter 60”). Except in contract cases, a demand over $75,000 must say only that damages exceed $75,000, and a demand of $75,000 or less must state the specific amount. Before taking a default on an “exceeds $75,000” petition, notify the defendant of the amount by return-receipt delivery at least 14 days before judgment is sought. (K.S.A. 60-207(c); 60-208(a)(2); 60-254(c))

docs.t: Kansas — Jury demand within 14 days or it is waived
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Jury demand within 14 days or it is waived: Serve a written jury demand no later than 14 days after the last pleading directed to the issue, and file it. A missing or unfiled demand waives jury trial, though the court may relieve an inadvertent waiver. (K.S.A. 60-238(b), (d))

docs.t: Kansas — No initial disclosures, but expert and funding disclosures are mandatory
docs.x: Kansas land mine. No initial disclosures, but expert and funding disclosures are mandatory: Kansas has no Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1) initial disclosures. Expert disclosures (identity, subject, substance of facts and opinions, and for retained experts a summary of grounds) are due at least 90 days before trial absent an order, and are filed with the court. Litigation funding agreements must be submitted in camera and disclosed by sworn statement within 30 days after the case starts or the agreement is signed. (K.S.A. 60-226(b)(3)(B), (b)(6))

docs.t: Kansas — Nonparty deposition timing tied to the case management conference
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Nonparty deposition timing tied to the case management conference: Without stipulation or leave, a nonparty may not be deposed before the case management conference (which must be held within 45 days after an answer, unless extended) unless the notice certifies with facts that the deponent will leave Kansas. If no conference is held within 45 days after the answer, the restriction lapses. (K.S.A. 60-216(b)(2); 60-230(a)(2)(A)(ii))

docs.t: Kansas — Document subpoenas need advance notice to all parties
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Document subpoenas need advance notice to all parties: A subpoena for documents or inspection that is not tied to a deposition may be served only after notice is served on every party. A records-only subpoena under 60-245a requires 14 days’ advance notice with a copy of the proposed subpoena, and any party objection blocks issuance without a court order. (K.S.A. 60-245(b); 60-245a(b)(1)(A))

docs.t: Kansas — Change-of-judge window is 7 days
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Change-of-judge window is 7 days: In prejudgment matters, a motion for change of judge must be filed within 7 days after pretrial or after written notice of the assigned judge, whichever is later, and each party gets only one change. The motion itself must not state grounds; an affidavit with grounds follows immediately if the judge refuses. (K.S.A. 20-311d(a); 20-311f)

docs.t: Kansas — Post-trial motions: 28 days, no extensions
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Post-trial motions: 28 days, no extensions: Renewed motions for judgment as a matter of law, motions to amend findings, new-trial motions, and motions to alter or amend must be filed within 28 days after entry of judgment, and the court has no power to extend those deadlines. (K.S.A. 60-206(b)(2); 60-250(b); 60-252(b); 60-259(b), (f))

docs.t: Kansas — The appeal clock starts at the filed journal entry, not the oral ruling
docs.x: Kansas land mine. The appeal clock starts at the filed journal entry, not the oral ruling: A judgment is not effective until a journal entry or judgment form is signed and filed; the 30-day notice of appeal runs from that entry, and the notice is filed in the district court. The only statutory extension is up to 30 days for excusable neglect based on not learning of the entry. (K.S.A. 60-258; 60-2103(a))

docs.t: Kansas — Cross-appeal in 21 days
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Cross-appeal in 21 days: An appellee who wants any ruling reviewed must file a notice of cross-appeal within 21 days after the notice of appeal was served on it and filed. (K.S.A. 60-2103(h))

docs.t: Kansas — Object to Court of Appeals jurisdiction within 30 days
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Object to Court of Appeals jurisdiction within 30 days: A motion to transfer a case from the Court of Appeals to the Supreme Court must be filed within 30 days after the notice of appeal is served on the appellee; failing to file waives any objection to Court of Appeals jurisdiction. (K.S.A. 20-3017)

docs.t: Kansas — Anti-SLAPP motion: 60 days, and fees are mandatory
docs.x: Kansas land mine. Anti-SLAPP motion: 60 days, and fees are mandatory: The motion to strike may be filed within 60 days of service of the most recent complaint (later only in the court’s discretion), and a hearing must occur within 30 days after service of the motion. A prevailing movant must be awarded fees and costs, and sanctions may reach the opposing lawyers and law firms. An appeal from denial requires notice within 14 days. (K.S.A. 60-5320(d), (f), (g))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Statute: Public Speech Protection Act
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Statute: Public Speech Protection Act: K.S.A. 60-5320, enacted 2016 (L. 2016, ch. 58, eff. July 1, 2016). It protects the exercise of free speech (a communication in connection with a public issue or issue of public interest, defined to include health or safety, environmental, economic or community well-being, government, public officials or figures, and marketplace goods or services), the right to petition (broadly defined, including communications in or about judicial, official, legislative, and executive proceedings), and the right of association. It is to be construed liberally. (K.S.A. 60-5320(a)-(c), (k))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Motion to strike: 60 days; hearing within 30 days
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Motion to strike: 60 days; hearing within 30 days: A party may move to strike a claim (including a counterclaim or cross-claim) that is based on, relates to, or responds to its protected activity. The motion may be filed within 60 days of service of the most recent complaint or later in the court’s discretion. A hearing must be held not more than 30 days after service of the motion. (K.S.A. 60-5320(c)(1), (d))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Burden shifting
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Burden shifting: The movant must make a prima facie showing that the claim concerns its exercise of speech, petition, or association. The burden then shifts to the responding party to establish a likelihood of prevailing by presenting substantial competent evidence of a prima facie case; if it does, the motion is denied. The court considers the pleadings and supporting and opposing affidavits. A determination that the responding party is likely to prevail is not admissible later and does not change the burden of proof. Unlike some states, there is no separate step letting the movant defeat the claim by proving a defense. (K.S.A. 60-5320(d))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Discovery and proceedings stayed
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Discovery and proceedings stayed: Filing the motion stays all discovery, motions, and other pending hearings until the ruling, except specified and limited discovery the court allows for good cause. (K.S.A. 60-5320(e))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Mandatory fees and sanctions
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Mandatory fees and sanctions: If the movant prevails, the court must award costs and reasonable attorney fees, without regard to state-law limits, plus additional relief, including sanctions on the responding party and its attorneys and law firms, needed to deter repetition. If the motion is frivolous or solely for delay, the court must award the responding party its fees and costs on the motion. A ruling against a government contractor must be sent to the head of the contracting government entity. (K.S.A. 60-5320(g), (j))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Appeal: 14 days; mandamus if no ruling
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Appeal: 14 days; mandamus if no ruling: The movant may file an interlocutory appeal from an order denying the motion if the notice of appeal is filed within 14 days after entry, or petition for mandamus if the trial court fails to rule in an expedited fashion. Trial-court proceedings are stayed pending the appeal. (K.S.A. 60-5320(f))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Exemptions
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Exemptions: Does not apply to enforcement actions brought by the Attorney General or a district or county attorney in the name of the State or a subdivision; claims against a person primarily selling or leasing goods or services over statements or conduct arising from a sale, lease, insurance product, or commercial transaction aimed at actual or potential customers (but this exemption does not reach claims based on dramatic, literary, musical, political, or artistic works, or newspaper or magazine articles); or claims under the Kansas insurance code or an insurance contract. (K.S.A. 60-5320(h)-(i))

docs.t: Kansas anti-SLAPP — Check case law before relying on the statute
docs.x: Kansas anti-SLAPP. Check case law before relying on the statute: The Revisor’s annotations list one appellate decision, holding that review of a ruling on the motion is de novo (Doe v. Kan. State Univ., 61 Kan. App. 2d 128 (2021)), and a 2024 law review article on federal collateral-order review of anti-SLAPP rulings. Later Kansas appellate decisions on the act’s scope or constitutionality, and whether federal courts in Kansas apply it, were not researched. (K.S.A. 60-5320 (Revisor annotations))

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (civil, district court to appellate court)
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil, district court to appellate court): 30 days from Entry of judgment (journal entry or judgment form signed and filed) (K.S.A. 60-2103(a); 60-258). Filed with the clerk of the district court. Extendable by up to 30 days only for excusable neglect based on failure to learn of the entry of judgment.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Appeal after a timely post-trial motion
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Appeal after a timely post-trial motion: 30 days from Entry of the order granting or denying a 60-250(b), 60-252(b), or 60-259 motion (for a new-trial motion, the order denying it) (K.S.A. 60-2103(a)). Full 30 days runs anew.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law: 28 days from Entry of judgment (or jury discharge if the issue was not decided by verdict) (K.S.A. 60-250(b)). Cannot be extended (60-206(b)(2)).

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Motion for new trial; motion to alter or amend
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Motion for new trial; motion to alter or amend: 28 days from Entry of judgment (K.S.A. 60-259(b), (f)). Cannot be extended. The court may order a new trial on its own within the same 28 days.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Motion to amend or add findings
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Motion to amend or add findings: 28 days from Entry of judgment (K.S.A. 60-252(b)). Cannot be extended.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Notice of cross-appeal
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Notice of cross-appeal: 21 days from Service and filing of the notice of appeal (K.S.A. 60-2103(h)).

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Application for permissive interlocutory appeal
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Application for permissive interlocutory appeal: 14 days from Entry of the order containing the district judge’s written certification (K.S.A. 60-2102(c)). Filed with the Court of Appeals; procedure set by Supreme Court rule (not collected).

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Application to appeal class-certification order
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Application to appeal class-certification order: 14 days from Entry of the order (K.S.A. 60-223(f)). No automatic stay.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Notice of appeal from denial of anti-SLAPP motion to strike
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Notice of appeal from denial of anti-SLAPP motion to strike: 14 days from Entry of the order denying the motion (K.S.A. 60-5320(f)). Trial-court proceedings are stayed pending the appeal.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Appeal from a non-lawyer district magistrate judge
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Appeal from a non-lawyer district magistrate judge: 14 days from Entry of the order or decision (K.S.A. 60-2103a(a)). Heard by a district judge, not the Court of Appeals.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Motion to transfer from Court of Appeals to Supreme Court
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Motion to transfer from Court of Appeals to Supreme Court: 30 days from Service of the notice of appeal on the appellee (K.S.A. 20-3017). Not filing waives any objection to Court of Appeals jurisdiction.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Petition for review in the Supreme Court
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Petition for review in the Supreme Court: 30 days from Date of the Court of Appeals decision (K.S.A. 20-3018(b)). A rehearing motion is not a prerequisite. Whether a rehearing motion affects this time is governed by Supreme Court rule (not collected).

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Appeal to Supreme Court from decision holding a statute unconstitutional under Kan. Const. art. 6
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Appeal to Supreme Court from decision holding a statute unconstitutional under Kan. Const. art. 6: 30 days from Filing of the preliminary or final decision (K.S.A. 60-2102(b)(1)).

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Appeal of local-government quasi-judicial order to district court
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Appeal of local-government quasi-judicial order to district court: 30 days from Entry of the order (K.S.A. 60-2101(d)). Only if no other appeal method is provided by law.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Suspension of order dissolving an injunction or provisional remedy
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Suspension of order dissolving an injunction or provisional remedy: 14 days from Order suspending it (K.S.A. 60-2103(d)(1)). Notice of appeal and approved supersedeas bond must be filed within the 14 days.

docs.t: Kansas appeal deadline — Automatic stay of execution
docs.x: Kansas appellate deadline. Automatic stay of execution: 14 days from Entry of judgment (K.S.A. 60-262(a)). Not for injunctions or receiverships.

docs.t: Kentucky — The appeal clock runs from the clerk’s docket notation of service, not entry
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. The appeal clock runs from the clerk’s docket notation of service, not entry: The 30 days to appeal run from the date of the clerk’s docket notation of service of the judgment under CR 77.04(2). A timely notice of appeal is jurisdictional, and a late one is dismissed. Failing to receive notice does not extend time, except that the trial court may add up to 10 days for excusable neglect in learning of entry. (RAP 2(A)(2)–(3), 3(A)(1)–(2), 3(C)–(D); CR 77.04(2), (4))

docs.t: Kentucky — Only CR 50.02, 52.02 and 59 motions toll; CR 60.02 does not
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Only CR 50.02, 52.02 and 59 motions toll; CR 60.02 does not: Time to appeal restarts for all parties only from the order disposing of the last timely CR 50.02, CR 52.02 or CR 59 motion, and not when a new trial is granted. No motion under any other civil rule tolls. To challenge the post-judgment order, you must file a new or amended notice of appeal. (RAP 3(E)(2), (E)(4))

docs.t: Kentucky — Cross-appeal: 10 days after the appeal deadline, and no extensions
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Cross-appeal: 10 days after the appeal deadline, and no extensions: A notice of cross-appeal is due no later than 10 days after the last day allowed for the notice of appeal. It does not run from service of the opponent’s notice. Courts may not extend or enlarge time under RAP 3, 4 or 17, even for excusable neglect. Without a cross-appeal, an appellee cannot seek to enlarge its own rights. (RAP 4(B)–(C), 6(C)–(D))

docs.t: Kentucky — Notice of appeal is not docketed until the fee is paid
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Notice of appeal is not docketed until the fee is paid: Pay the fee to the clerk of the court being appealed from when you tender the notice. The notice is not docketed or noted as filed until payment, unless an in forma pauperis motion accompanies it. The fee is $150 for appeals to the Court of Appeals or Supreme Court and $60 for district court appeals, as in the 2022 text. Check for later fee orders. (RAP 2(I) (AO 2026-01), 3(A)(3), 13(B), 48(B)(4))

docs.t: Kentucky — Temporary injunction rulings: 20 days to move the Court of Appeals
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Temporary injunction rulings: 20 days to move the Court of Appeals: There is no appellate review of a CR 65.03 restraining order. A party hurt by an order granting, denying, modifying or dissolving a temporary injunction must move the Court of Appeals within 20 days of entry. Further review in the Supreme Court is due within 10 days and requires extraordinary cause. Rulings under RAP 20 are not reconsidered. The old CR 65.07–65.09 procedures were deleted. (RAP 20(A), (B), (E), (F)(1); AO 2022-49 § II)

docs.t: Kentucky — Anti-SLAPP: 60 days from service, automatic stay, and mandatory fees
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Anti-SLAPP: 60 days from service, automatic stay, and mandatory fees: A defendant who waits past 60 days after service needs good cause to file the special motion. Plaintiffs should note that filing the motion stays discovery automatically, and a losing plaintiff pays the movant’s fees and expenses. (KRS 454.464, 454.466(1), 454.478(1))

docs.t: Kentucky — Pro hac vice lapses if the annual renewal goes unpaid
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Pro hac vice lapses if the annual renewal goes unpaid: The per-case fee recurs on each anniversary of admission while the case continues. Thirty days after a missed payment, the lawyer is suspended from appearing in every Kentucky pro hac vice case. Kentucky co-counsel must tell the court. (SCR 3.030(3)(a)–(b))

docs.t: Kentucky — eFiling deadline is midnight in the receiving court’s time zone; e-service adds 3 days
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. eFiling deadline is midnight in the receiving court’s time zone; e-service adds 3 days: An eFiling is filed when the system’s Notice of Electronic Filing (NEF) says it is. It must be completed before midnight in the time zone of the receiving court, and a judge may set an earlier time. Kentucky courts sit in both the Eastern and Central time zones. Emailing a document to the clerk or judge is not filing. Electronic service is treated like mail service under CR 6.05, which adds 3 days. Fix a document the clerk returns within 2 business days to keep the original filing time. (eFiling Rules §§ 8(2)(a)–(c), 8(3)(b), 13(7) (AO 2025-02))

docs.t: Kentucky — Appellate briefs: paper-style formatting, colored covers, word-count certificate
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Appellate briefs: paper-style formatting, colored covers, word-count certificate: Briefs need a 1½-inch left margin and 12-point text and footnotes, and must be bound at the left. Covers are color-coded: red for appellant, blue for appellee, yellow for reply. In the Court of Appeals, initial and response briefs are limited to 8,750 words or 20 computer-generated pages, and replies to 1,750 words or 4 pages. A computer-generated brief over the page limit needs a RAP 15 word-count certificate. Briefs must start the argument with a statement showing how each issue was preserved, with record cites. (RAP 15(C), 31(A), (C)(2), (G)(2) (AO 2026-01), 32(A)(4))

docs.t: Kentucky — If the appellee does not file a brief, the court may treat it as a confession of error
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. If the appellee does not file a brief, the court may treat it as a confession of error: If the appellee’s brief is late, the court may accept the appellant’s statement of facts and issues, may reverse if the appellant’s brief reasonably appears to support reversal, or may treat the failure as a confession of error and reverse without reaching the merits. (RAP 31(H)(3))

docs.t: Kentucky — Citing unpublished Kentucky opinions takes four conditions and the case number
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Citing unpublished Kentucky opinions takes four conditions and the case number: You may cite a ‘Not To Be Published’ Kentucky opinion only if all four conditions hold: it was rendered after January 1, 2003; it is final; no published opinion adequately addresses the point; and you say it is not binding. Give the style, date and case number. Unpublished out-of-state opinions need a URL or a full copy in the appendix. (RAP 41(A), (C))

docs.t: Kentucky — Court of Appeals prehearing conference: 20-day motion window that changes the briefing clock
docs.x: Kentucky land mine. Court of Appeals prehearing conference: 20-day motion window that changes the briefing clock: Since April 1, 2026, a prehearing conference in civil appeals is by optional motion with a prehearing statement, filed within 20 days of the notice of appeal or cross-appeal. Some case types are excluded. Further steps do not run until the Court of Appeals orders. If no motion is filed, the time runs from the clerk’s notice saying so. Record designation and certification deadlines are keyed to the end of the prehearing procedure, and RAP 24 and 26 still cite the pre-2026 numbering, so confirm dates with the clerk. (RAP 22(A)–(B) (AO 2026-01); RAP 24(A)(1)(b), 26(B)(4))

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Kentucky has an anti-SLAPP statute: KRS 454.460–454.478 (2022)
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Kentucky has an anti-SLAPP statute: KRS 454.460–454.478 (2022): Kentucky enacted a Uniform Public Expression Protection Act–style statute in 2022 Ky. Acts ch. 233, effective July 14, 2022. It provides a ‘special motion for expedited relief’ to dismiss a cause of action in whole or in part. The statute has no short title, so ‘UPEPA’ is a descriptive label. Cite the sections themselves. (KRS 454.460–454.478; 2022 Ky. Acts ch. 233)

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Scope: government proceedings and speech on matters of public concern
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Scope: government proceedings and speech on matters of public concern: The statute covers claims based on three kinds of activity: (a) communication in a legislative, executive, judicial, administrative, or other governmental proceeding; (b) communication on an issue under consideration in such a proceeding; and (c) exercise of free speech, press, assembly, petition, or association rights under the U.S. or Kentucky Constitution on a matter of public concern. ‘Matter of public concern’ is defined in KRS 454.460(4). It excludes ten categories (KRS 454.462(2)(a)). These include claims against or by government units in certain capacities, commercial speech about the defendant’s own goods or services, real-property claims, bodily injury, wrongful death, and survival claims, insurance-code and insurance-contract claims, common-law fraud, KRS Chapters 401–407, employment st

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Deadline: 60 days from service of the pleading
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Deadline: 60 days from service of the pleading: File the special motion no later than 60 days after being served with the complaint, crossclaim, counterclaim, third-party claim, or other pleading asserting the claim. A later filing requires a showing of good cause. (KRS 454.464)

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Automatic stay of everything between the movant and respondent
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Automatic stay of everything between the movant and respondent: Filing the motion stays all other proceedings between the moving and responding parties, including discovery and pending hearings and motions. On motion, the court may also stay matters involving other parties. The stay lasts until the ruling and the expiration of the time to appeal. If anyone appeals, all proceedings between all parties are stayed until the appeal ends. The court must allow limited discovery if a party shows that specific information is necessary to the KRS 454.472(1) burdens and is not reasonably available otherwise. Fee motions, voluntary dismissals, motions to sever, unrelated motions (for good cause), and injunctions against imminent public-health or public-safety threats are not blocked by the stay. (KRS 454.466)

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Hearing within 60 days; ruling within 60 days after the hearing
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Hearing within 60 days; ruling within 60 days after the hearing: The court must hear the motion within 60 days after filing, unless it orders a later hearing to allow limited discovery (then within 60 days of that order) or for good cause. It must rule within 60 days after the hearing. The court considers the pleadings, the motion, any response or reply, and any evidence admissible on summary judgment. (KRS 454.468, 454.470, 454.474)

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Three-step test; dismissal is with prejudice
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Three-step test; dismissal is with prejudice: The court must dismiss with prejudice if three things are true. First, the movant shows the statute applies under KRS 454.462(1). Second, the respondent fails to show an exclusion applies under KRS 454.462(2). Third, either the respondent fails to establish a prima facie case on each essential element, or the movant shows a failure to state a claim or no genuine issue of material fact. A voluntary dismissal without prejudice does not defeat the motion or the fee claim. A voluntary dismissal with prejudice makes the movant the prevailing party for fees. (KRS 454.472)

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Immediate appeal as of right by either side
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Immediate appeal as of right by either side: Any party may appeal as of right from an order granting or denying the motion in whole or in part. The statute says the appeal is filed ‘in accordance with the Kentucky Rules of Civil Procedure’. Since January 1, 2023, appellate procedure has been in the Rules of Appellate Procedure (RAP 1(A); CR 1(2)), so expect a RAP 3 notice of appeal within 30 days. No collected text addresses that wording mismatch. (KRS 454.476; RAP 3(A)(1))

docs.t: Kentucky anti-SLAPP — Fees: mandatory for a winning movant; for a respondent only if the motion lacked good cause
docs.x: Kentucky anti-SLAPP. Fees: mandatory for a winning movant; for a respondent only if the motion lacked good cause: On the motion or an appeal of the order, the court shall award court costs, reasonable attorney’s fees, and reasonable litigation expenses related to the motion. A prevailing movant always gets them. A prevailing respondent gets them only if the court finds the motion was brought without good cause. (KRS 454.478)

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (civil)
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil): 30 days from Clerk’s docket notation of service of the judgment or order (CR 77.04(2)) (RAP 3(A)(1)–(2)). Jurisdictional; cannot be extended except up to 10 extra days for excusable neglect in learning of entry (RAP 3(D)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Extension for failure to learn of entry
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Extension for failure to learn of entry: 10 days from Expiration of the original appeal time (RAP 3(D)). Granted by the trial court on excusable neglect.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Notice of appeal after a tolling motion
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Notice of appeal after a tolling motion: 30 days from Docket notation of service of the order disposing of the last CR 50.02, 52.02 or 59 motion (RAP 3(E)(2), (4)). Other motions, including CR 60.02, do not toll.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Notice of cross-appeal
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Notice of cross-appeal: 10 days from Last day allowed for filing the notice of appeal (RAP 4(B)). No extension (RAP 6(C)–(D)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Additional cross-appeal
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Additional cross-appeal: 10 days from Filing of the notice of cross-appeal that first affects the party (RAP 4(E)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion to transfer to Supreme Court
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion to transfer to Supreme Court: 10 days from Filing of notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals (RAP 17(A)). No extension; response 10 days.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Pay fee or appeal denial of in forma pauperis
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Pay fee or appeal denial of in forma pauperis: 30 days from Denial of the in forma pauperis motion (RAP 3(A)(3)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion for prehearing conference (Court of Appeals civil)
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion for prehearing conference (Court of Appeals civil): 20 days from Notice of appeal (or notice of cross-appeal) (RAP 22(A)(1) (AO 2026-01)). Optional since April 1, 2026; other parties respond within 10 days (RAP 22(C)(3)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Designation of recordings for the record
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Designation of recordings for the record: 10 days from Notice of appeal (or order ending prehearing procedure if RAP 22 applies) (RAP 24(A)(1)(b)). Counter-designation 10 days after (RAP 24(A)(2)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Clerk certifies record
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Clerk certifies record: 30 days from First notice of appeal (or order ending prehearing procedure) (RAP 26(B)(4)). Clerk duty; may be extended on motion.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 60 days from Docket notation of clerk’s notice of certification of the record (or order granting discretionary review) (RAP 30(C)(1)(a)). Expedited appeals: 30 days (RAP 30(E)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 60 days from Filing of appellant’s brief (RAP 30(C)(1)(b)). Expedited: 30 days.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Reply brief: 15 days from Filing of last appellee’s brief (or when due, if replying to several) (RAP 30(C)(1)(c) (AO 2026-01)). Expedited: 10 days.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Combined appellee/cross-appellant brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Combined appellee/cross-appellant brief: 60 days from Filing of appellant’s brief (RAP 30(C)(2)(b)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Combined appellant reply/cross-appellee brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Combined appellant reply/cross-appellee brief: 60 days from Last appellee brief filed or due (RAP 30(C)(2)(c)). Cross-appellant reply 15 days after (RAP 30(C)(2)(d)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Amicus motion and brief
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Amicus motion and brief: 15 days from Appellant’s brief filed or due, whichever is later (RAP 34(B)(2)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Response to a motion
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Response to a motion: 10 days from Filing of the motion (RAP 7(C) (AO 2026-01)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Corrected document after deficiency notice
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Corrected document after deficiency notice: 10 days from Date of the deficiency notice (RAP 5(F)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion for relief from temporary-injunction order
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion for relief from temporary-injunction order: 20 days from Entry of the circuit court’s interlocutory order (RAP 20(B)). Response 10 days.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Supreme Court review of RAP 20/21 ruling
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Supreme Court review of RAP 20/21 ruling: 10 days from Entry of the Court of Appeals order (RAP 20(F)(1); RAP 21(B)). Discretionary; extraordinary cause.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing, modification, extension or publication
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing, modification, extension or publication: 20 days from Date the opinion was issued (RAP 43(B)(3)). Response 20 days after petition.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion to reconsider an order
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion to reconsider an order: 20 days from Entry of the order (RAP 43(D)(1)). Not available for RAP 17, 20, 21 or 44 orders.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion for discretionary review (Supreme Court)
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion for discretionary review (Supreme Court): 30 days from Court of Appeals decision (or denial of, or decision on, rehearing/reconsideration) (RAP 44(B)(2)). Response 30 days; no enlargement after the fact (RAP 6(D)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Motion for discretionary review (Court of Appeals, district-court cases)
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Motion for discretionary review (Court of Appeals, district-court cases): 30 days from Entry of the circuit court’s appellate judgment (RAP 44(B)(1)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Cross-motion for discretionary review
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Cross-motion for discretionary review: 10 days from Order granting the motion for discretionary review (RAP 46(A)). Response 10 days.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Statement of appeal (district court to circuit court)
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Statement of appeal (district court to circuit court): 30 days from Filing of the notice of appeal (RAP 48(F)(1)). Counterstatement 30 days after statement (RAP 48(F)(2)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Response to original action (writ) petition
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Response to original action (writ) petition: 20 days from Filing of the petition (RAP 60(D)).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Appeal of Court of Appeals final order in original action
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Appeal of Court of Appeals final order in original action: 30 days from Entry of the judgment or order (RAP 60(I)(2)). Filed with the Court of Appeals clerk.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Anti-SLAPP special motion
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Anti-SLAPP special motion: 60 days from Service of the pleading asserting the claim (KRS 454.464). Later only for good cause; order is appealable as of right (KRS 454.476).

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Supreme Court opinion becomes final
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Supreme Court opinion becomes final: 21 days from Rendition (RAP 40(G)(1)). Absent timely RAP 43 petition.

docs.t: Kentucky appeal deadline — Court of Appeals opinion becomes final
docs.x: Kentucky appellate deadline. Court of Appeals opinion becomes final: 31 days from Rendition (RAP 40(G)(1)). Absent timely RAP 43 petition or RAP 44 motion.

docs.t: Louisiana — No motion to dismiss: plead the right exception, at the right time, or lose it
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. No motion to dismiss: plead the right exception, at the right time, or lose it: Rule 12-style defenses are raised by exception. Declinatory (insufficient citation or service, including failure to request service within 90 days; lis pendens; improper venue; lack of personal jurisdiction) and dilatory exceptions (prematurity, vagueness, improper cumulation, lack of capacity, and others) must be filed together, before or in the answer and before any other pleading seeking relief, and before a default is signed. Objections not pleaded are waived, including venue. The peremptory exception (prescription, no cause of action, no right of action, res judicata, subject-matter jurisdiction, and others) can be filed until submission for decision, and no evidence is allowed on no cause of action. (La. C.C.P. arts. 44(C), 922, 925–928, 931)

docs.t: Louisiana — Abandonment: three years without a step ends the case automatically
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Abandonment: three years without a step ends the case automatically: A suit is abandoned, without any order, if no party takes a step in the trial court for three years; formal discovery served on a party, filed or not, counts. A 2026 amendment (Acts 2026, No. 127) requires the mover’s affidavit to list record filings for the prior three years and written communications in the final year, and sets 30 days from sheriff’s service to move to set aside and 60 days to appeal. Abandonment also wipes out the interruption of prescription the suit created (Civil Code art. 3463(B)), except that dismissal of a suit on a conventional obligation still interrupts prescription under art. 561(L). Calendar a step at least every two and a half years. (La. C.C.P. art. 561; La. Civ. Code art. 3463(B))

docs.t: Louisiana — Prescription: tort claims now two years, but check the old one-year rule for older injuries
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Prescription: tort claims now two years, but check the old one-year rule for older injuries: Acts 2024, No. 423 repealed Civil Code arts. 3492 and 3493 effective July 1, 2024 and enacted art. 3493.1: delictual actions prescribe in two years from the day injury or damage is sustained (with a special start for damage to immovables in art. 3493.2). Claims arising before July 1, 2024 may still be governed by the former one-year period; the Act’s transition provision was not collected, so confirm it before relying on two years for older claims. Prescription must be specially pleaded; the court will not raise it except in defaults. Filing in an incompetent court or improper venue interrupts prescription only as to defendants served within the period (with a 7-day suspension for a competent court of improper venue, added in 2025). (La. Civ. Code arts. 3462, 3493.1, 3493.2;

docs.t: Louisiana — Request service within 90 days, and pay the clerk
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Request service within 90 days, and pay the clerk: Service of citation must be requested on every named defendant within 90 days of filing (or of an amended petition adding the defendant), and the clerk’s service fees must be paid within that period (or 30 days after a statement of additional fees). A defendant can obtain dismissal without prejudice by declinatory exception or contradictory motion unless good cause is shown, and voluntary or involuntary dismissal can erase the interruption of prescription. Service is by the sheriff; a private process server requires a court appointment after the sheriff fails for 10 days. (La. C.C.P. arts. 1201(C)–(E), 1293, 1672(C); La. Civ. Code art. 3463(B))

docs.t: Louisiana — Devolutive vs. suspensive appeal: 60 days or 30 days plus bond
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Devolutive vs. suspensive appeal: 60 days or 30 days plus bond: You appeal by obtaining an order of appeal from the trial court, not by filing a notice. A devolutive appeal (no stay, no bond) is due within 60 days, and a suspensive appeal (stays execution) within 30 days, with the security posted within the same 30 days, both counted from the end of the 7-day new-trial/JNOV delay (exclusive of legal holidays) or from mailing of notice denying such a motion. Miss the 30 days and the judgment can be executed. Appellees wanting relief must answer the appeal within 15 days after the return day or lodging. (La. C.C.P. arts. 1974, 2087, 2121, 2123, 2124, 2133, 2252)

docs.t: Louisiana — Partial rulings are interlocutory: use a writ, fast
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Partial rulings are interlocutory: use a writ, fast: A judgment, partial summary judgment, or sustained exception disposing of fewer than all claims, issues, or theories by or against a party is interlocutory under art. 1915(C) as amended by Acts 2025, No. 250, with no designation procedure in the current text. Review is by supervisory writ: give notice of intent and get a return date, which may not exceed 30 days from notice of the ruling. Denials of exceptions and of summary judgment are likewise reviewed only by writ (and a summary-judgment denial is never appealable). (La. C.C.P. arts. 968, 1914, 1915(C), 2083(C); Unif. R. Ct. App. 4-2, 4-3)

docs.t: Louisiana — Never plead a dollar amount; know the jury threshold and bond
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Never plead a dollar amount; know the jury threshold and bond: A petition may not state a specific amount of damages (except in suits on contracts, notes, open accounts, and similar claims); use a general allegation that the claim exceeds or is less than a threshold when it matters, such as for federal diversity or the jury right. A specific amount is struck on motion and can bring fees. No jury where no plaintiff’s claim exceeds $10,000; a jury demand is due within 10 days after service of the last pleading on a jury issue and requires a bond (or a $5,000 cash deposit within 60 days in tort cases stipulated between $10,000 and $50,000). (La. C.C.P. arts. 893, 1732, 1733, 1734)

docs.t: Louisiana — Summary judgment has hard, fixed deadlines
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Summary judgment has hard, fixed deadlines: Unless the court extends and all parties agree: the motion and supporting documents must be filed and served at least 65 days before trial, the opposition at least 15 days before the hearing, and the reply at least 5 days before (counting legal holidays). The hearing must be set at least 30 days after filing and 30 days before trial, and judgment rendered at least 20 days before trial. Only listed kinds of documents count, and evidentiary objections go in the opposition or reply. Documents filed late are not considered. (La. C.C.P. art. 966(A)(4), (B), (C), (D)(2))

docs.t: Louisiana — Answer in 21 days; defaults move fast and need only 7 days’ notice in some cases
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Answer in 21 days; defaults move fast and need only 7 days’ notice in some cases: The answer is due 21 days after service of citation (30 if discovery was served with the petition). There is no preliminary default: once the delay runs, the plaintiff may obtain a default judgment on a prima facie case. Notice of intent to take a default is required, at least 7 days before, only if the defendant appeared of record, the defendant’s lawyer wrote to the plaintiff about the case, or it is a tort case. A defendant may still answer any time before the default is signed. New-trial delays then run 7 days from notice. (La. C.C.P. arts. 1001, 1002, 1702(A), 1974)

docs.t: Louisiana — District court filing: paper in person or e-file only since January 1, 2026
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. District court filing: paper in person or e-file only since January 1, 2026: Since January 1, 2026, attorneys’ filings in district court may be made only in person on paper or electronically through the clerk’s system or the Louisiana Clerks’ Remote Access Authority (with listed original documents still allowed by mail or courier), and statutory fax filing ended January 1, 2026. Filings must omit the first five digits of SSNs, tax and account numbers, and other protected information. Do not plan to fax a motion for appeal or new trial on the last day. (La. C.C.P. art. 253(B)(2)–(3); La. R.S. 13:850(A))

docs.t: Louisiana — Pro hac vice starts at the Disciplinary Board and closes 30 days before trial
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Pro hac vice starts at the Disciplinary Board and closes 30 days before trial: Before moving the court, the out-of-state lawyer must file a verified application with the Louisiana Attorney Disciplinary Board and pay $450, then obtain Disciplinary Counsel’s letter, which Louisiana counsel attaches to an ex parte motion served on all parties. Any party or Disciplinary Counsel may object within 20 days. Absent extraordinary circumstances explained in the motion, courts will not consider a motion filed within 30 days of trial or hearing. Louisiana counsel must remain associated and responsible throughout. (La. Sup. Ct. R. XVII, § 13(A)(1)–(4); La. R.S. 37:214)

docs.t: Louisiana — Local motion practice: 15-day memoranda and judgment circulation
docs.x: Louisiana land mine. Local motion practice: 15-day memoranda and judgment circulation: Under the statewide District Court Rules, the mover’s memorandum must be received by all parties 15 calendar days before the hearing and the opposition 8 calendar days before; replies must arrive by 4:00 p.m. leaving one full working day before the hearing. Proposed judgments not signed at the hearing must be circulated at least 5 working days before presentation, with a Rule 9.5(b) certificate. Late memoranda can cost oral argument and the other side’s costs. (La. Dist. Ct. R. 9.5(b), 9.8(c), 9.9(b)–(e))

docs.t: Louisiana anti-SLAPP — Louisiana has an anti-SLAPP procedure: the special motion to strike, La. C.C.P. art. 971
docs.x: Louisiana anti-SLAPP. Louisiana has an anti-SLAPP procedure: the special motion to strike, La. C.C.P. art. 971: Scope: a cause of action against a person arising from any act in furtherance of that person’s right of petition or free speech under the U.S. or Louisiana Constitution in connection with a public issue. Covered acts include statements before, or in connection with an issue under review by, a legislative, executive, or judicial body or other official proceeding; statements in a place open to the public or a public forum on an issue of public interest; and any other conduct furthering petition or speech rights on a public issue or issue of public interest. Standard: the motion is granted unless the court determines that the plaintiff has established a probability of success on the claim. The court considers the pleadings and supporting and opposing affidavits. A finding that the

docs.t: Louisiana anti-SLAPP — Deadline: 90 days from service; hearing within 30 days; discovery stayed
docs.x: Louisiana anti-SLAPP. Deadline: 90 days from service; hearing within 30 days; discovery stayed: File within 90 days of service of the petition, or later in the court’s discretion on terms it sets. If the plaintiff voluntarily dismisses before the answer delay runs, the defendant keeps the right to file the motion within the same 90 days, and it is heard under art. 971. The motion is to be noticed for hearing not more than 30 days after service unless docket conditions require a later hearing. All discovery is stayed when notice of the motion is filed, until notice of entry of the order ruling on it; the court may allow specified discovery on noticed motion for good cause. (La. C.C.P. art. 971(C)(1)–(3), (D))

docs.t: Louisiana anti-SLAPP — Fees go to the prevailing party, either side
docs.x: Louisiana anti-SLAPP. Fees go to the prevailing party, either side: A prevailing party on a special motion to strike “shall be awarded” reasonable attorney fees and costs. The text is not limited to a prevailing defendant, so a plaintiff who defeats the motion can also recover. (La. C.C.P. art. 971(B))

docs.t: Louisiana anti-SLAPP — Appeal: no special appeal rule in the current article
docs.x: Louisiana anti-SLAPP. Appeal: no special appeal rule in the current article: The current text of art. 971 (last amended by Acts 2012, No. 449) contains no provision of its own on appeal. Whether a ruling is appealable therefore turns on the general rules: a judgment granting the motion and dismissing the claims is a final judgment (or a partial final judgment needing designation under art. 1915(B) if claims remain), while a denial is interlocutory and is reviewed by supervisory writ under art. 2083(C). Confirm with current case law before relying on this. (La. C.C.P. arts. 971, 1915, 2083 (appeal route is Consi’s inference from the text))

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Motion for new trial
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Motion for new trial: 7 days from Clerk’s mailing or delivery in open court, or sheriff’s service, of notice of judgment (art. 1913) (La. C.C.P. art. 1974). Exclusive of legal holidays. Tolls appeal delays for all parties.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Motion for JNOV
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Motion for JNOV: 7 days from Notice of judgment (or jury discharge if no verdict) (La. C.C.P. art. 1811(A)). Exclusive of legal holidays.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Devolutive appeal (order of appeal)
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Devolutive appeal (order of appeal): 60 days from Expiry of new-trial/JNOV delay, or mailing of notice of denial of a timely motion (La. C.C.P. art. 2087(A)). No bond. Does not stay execution.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Suspensive appeal (order of appeal and security)
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Suspensive appeal (order of appeal and security): 30 days from Expiry of new-trial/JNOV delay, or mailing of notice of denial of a timely motion (La. C.C.P. art. 2123(A)). Security must also be furnished within the 30 days; late bond allows conversion to devolutive.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Appellee’s own devolutive appeal
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Appellee’s own devolutive appeal: 10 days from Clerk’s mailing of notice of the first devolutive appeal (La. C.C.P. art. 2087(B)). Or within the normal 60 days, whichever is later.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Answer to appeal (cross-relief)
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Answer to appeal (cross-relief): 15 days from Return day or lodging of the record, whichever is later (La. C.C.P. art. 2133(A)). Required to obtain any change in the judgment.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Pay estimated appeal costs
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Pay estimated appeal costs: 20 days from Transmission of the clerk’s notice of estimated costs (La. C.C.P. art. 2126). One extension of up to 20 days for good cause.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Designate partial record
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Designate partial record: 10 days from Transmission of notice of estimated costs (La. C.C.P. art. 2128). Other parties may counter-designate within 14 days after service.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Return day
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Return day: 30 days from Payment of estimated costs (La. C.C.P. art. 2125). 45 days if testimony must be transcribed; one trial-court extension of up to 30 days.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Motion to dismiss appeal for appellant’s irregularity
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Motion to dismiss appeal for appellant’s irregularity: 3 days from Return day or lodging, whichever is later (La. C.C.P. art. 2161). Exclusive of holidays.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Appellant’s brief
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Appellant’s brief: 25 days from Lodging of the record (Unif. R. Ct. App. 2-12.7). Calendar days.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief: 45 days from Lodging of the record (Unif. R. Ct. App. 2-12.7). Extended 20 days beyond any extension granted to the appellant.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Reply brief: 10 days from Filing of appellee’s brief (Unif. R. Ct. App. 2-12.7). Confined to rebuttal.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Brief after abandonment notice
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Brief after abandonment notice: 30 days from Clerk’s transmission of the abandonment notice (Unif. R. Ct. App. 2-8.6). Otherwise the appeal is subject to dismissal as abandoned.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Supervisory writ application (civil)
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Supervisory writ application (civil): 30 days from Notice of the interlocutory judgment under art. 1914 (Unif. R. Ct. App. 4-3). Maximum; the actual deadline is the return date the judge sets, which may be shorter.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Preliminary-injunction appeal
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Preliminary-injunction appeal: 15 days from Date of the order or judgment (La. C.C.P. art. 3612(C)). Bond, if required, also within 15 days. No appeal from TRO orders.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Court of appeal rehearing
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Court of appeal rehearing: 14 days from Transmission of notice of judgment (La. C.C.P. art. 2166(A); Unif. R. Ct. App. 2-18.2). No extensions.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Supreme Court certiorari
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Supreme Court certiorari: 30 days from Transmission of the court of appeal’s notice of judgment, or of notice of denial of rehearing (La. C.C.P. art. 2166(A)–(C)). Second applicant: later of 30 days or 10 days after notice of the first application.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Opposition to Supreme Court writ application
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Opposition to Supreme Court writ application: 30 days from Date of the Court’s acknowledgment letter (La. Sup. Ct. R. X, § 5). No extensions absent clear and convincing proof of circumstances beyond the party’s control.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Supreme Court rehearing
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Supreme Court rehearing: 14 days from Transmission of notice of judgment (La. C.C.P. art. 2167(A)). Only after a grant of writ, appeal, or other proceeding.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — City or parish court appeal
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. City or parish court appeal: 10 days from Judgment, or service of notice of judgment when required (La. C.C.P. art. 5002). To the court of appeal.

docs.t: Louisiana appeal deadline — Suspensive appeal from eviction
docs.x: Louisiana appellate deadline. Suspensive appeal from eviction: 1 days from Rendition of judgment of eviction (La. C.C.P. art. 4735). 24 hours; also requires a sworn answer pleading an affirmative defense.

docs.t: Maryland — The Maryland Rules, not the Federal Rules
docs.x: Maryland land mine. The Maryland Rules, not the Federal Rules: Circuit court civil practice is under Title 2 of the Maryland Rules, District Court practice under Title 3, and appeals under Title 8. Their numbering and deadlines differ from the federal rules. These rules have the force of law. (Rule text was not collected for this page; read the current Rules.) (Md. Const. art. IV, § 18(a); Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 1-201)

docs.t: Maryland — Two different trial courts, and the $5,000 / $30,000 lines
docs.x: Maryland land mine. Two different trial courts, and the $5,000 / $30,000 lines: The District Court has exclusive jurisdiction over contract and tort claims up to $30,000 and over small claims up to $5,000. Above $5,000 (except replevin, landlord-tenant and certain other cases) the plaintiff may choose the District Court or the circuit court. Claims for equity relief (outside the listed exceptions), title to real property, and declaratory judgments must go to the circuit court. The $30,000 cap changes under laws effective June 30, 2028 and 2029; check the version in effect. (Cts. & Jud. Proc. §§ 4-401(1), 4-402(a)-(d), 4-405)

docs.t: Maryland — District Court appeal: 30 days, filed in the District Court, often de novo
docs.x: Maryland land mine. District Court appeal: 30 days, filed in the District Court, often de novo: Appeals from District Court civil judgments go to the circuit court for the same county (or Baltimore City), not to the Appellate Court. File the order for appeal with the District Court clerk within 30 days of the final judgment; certain landlord-tenant cases have shorter, section-specific times.
